document.title: Andropov handwritten memo to Brezhnev, early December 1979
document.authors: Yuri Andropov (KGB), transcribed by Anatoly Dobrynin from the Kremlin Archive (APRF)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan, 1979: Not Trump’s Terrorists, Nor Zbig’s Warm Water Ports | National Security Archive
document.note: Known only because Dobrynin transcribed it at the Presidential Archive in 1995. It is the KGB head's direct recommendation to Brezhnev that the Soviets replace Afghan Communist leader Amin because he might go over to the Americans.

events.description: April revolution in Afghanistan referenced as the achievement to defend.
Murder of Taraki (memo says September; editorial note corrects to October 8) following Amin's coup.
Andropov writes handwritten memo to Brezhnev proposing assistance to Karmal and Sarwari and forces along the border.
Dobrynin reads the memo aloud at Nobel Institute conference in Lysebu.
Amin's mass arrests: 500 arrested, 300 reportedly killed.
April revolution in Afghanistan, referenced as achievements to be defended.
Murder of Nur Muhammad Taraki following a coup (memo says September; editor corrects to October 8).
Amin carried out mass arrests: 500 arrested, 300 reportedly killed.
Soviet consultations with Babrak Karmal and Sarwari, who presented an anti-Amin plan and asked for assistance.
Andropov's handwritten memo to Brezhnev proposing a group of forces along the border and possible military assistance in Afghanistan.
Dobrynin read the memo aloud at the Nobel Institute conference.

key_claims: Andropov told Brezhnev that Amin's repressions had disorganized the Afghan government, army and state apparatus.
The KGB claimed Amin had secret contacts with the US chargé d'affaires and might reorient toward the West.
Amin allegedly promised tribal leaders to distance Afghanistan from the USSR and pursue neutrality.
Babrak Karmal and Sarwari presented a plan to move against Amin and asked for Soviet assistance, including military help.
Andropov proposed using two battalions in Kabul and massing forces along the border as an emergency measure.
